rows: CR-01
NDIA-ICT-ING-001
1. Purpose, authority and permitted exchange
Statutory purpose and lawful information exchange

NDIA integrations must be used only where they support NDIA statutory functions or an approved data sharing purpose, have a documented lawful authority, and enforce technical and procedural controls that prevent unauthorised collection, use, disclosure, caching, transformation, reuse or exchange of protected Agency information and barred data.
Applies to all APIs, files, events, data requests and outbound disclosures involving NDIA, participant, provider, plan, payment, review or Scheme information.

NDIA-ICT-ING-002
2. Governance, risk ownership and accountability
Governance, risk ownership and shared accountability

Every integration must have named business, system and security risk owners, be assessed against NDIA's approved governance arrangements and enterprise risk appetite, and allocate shared risk, control, monitoring, training, escalation and review responsibilities across NDIA and connected partners.
Applies to all material integrations, with heightened attention for provider, partner, Commonwealth, state or territory and outsourced connections.

3. Secure lifecycle and authorisation gates
Security lifecycle, authorisation, asset register and change control

Integrations must follow an ISM-aligned secure lifecycle from design to decommissioning, document architecture, control mapping and risk assessment, meet the approved Essential Eight target or obtain formal risk acceptance, and must not operate or materially change until residual risk is accepted by the Authorising Officer and the integration is recorded in the authorised systems or interface register.
Applies before production, reauthorisation and material change, and throughout operation, including legacy and internet-facing integration components.

4. Classification, markings and caveats
Classification, protective markings, metadata and caveat handling

Integration payloads, messages, records, logs and metadata must preserve security classifications, protective markings, caveats and access-restriction metadata, and must enforce need-to-know, clearance or eligibility, routing and recipient controls appropriate to the highest sensitivity or classification of the data, including AUSTEO, AGAO and foreign-origin information.
Applies where integrations process security classified, caveated, access-restricted or protectively marked information, including email or message notifications.

NDIA-ICT-ING-005
5. Sharing agreements and cross-border exchange
Information-sharing agreements, DATA Scheme controls and foreign/cross-border exchange

Before sharing data through an integration with another government, external, foreign or international party, NDIA must confirm the lawful sharing pathway, approved agreement or Data Sharing Agreement, participant accreditation where required, cross-border safeguards, foreign-interference and sovereignty risk treatment, authorised recipients, purpose, controls, retention and incident obligations, and must implement these requirements in technical release gates.
Applies to domestic intergovernmental, external, foreign, international and DATA Scheme integrations, and to overseas storage, routing or access to NDIA information.

NDIA-ICT-ING-006
6. Privacy and sensitive identifiers
Privacy, personal information, identifiers and sensitive health/identity data

Integrations involving personal information, health information, healthcare identifiers, government identifiers, Digital ID attributes or biometric and restricted identity data must complete privacy-by-design assessment, collect, use or disclose only approved fields for an authorised purpose, issue required notices or consent controls, protect information in transit, at rest and in logs, limit retention or de-identify it, restrict and review access, and prohibit My Health Record or restricted data handling unless expressly authorised and approved.
Applies to all integrations that collect, store, transform, match, identify, disclose, route or access personal, health, identifier or identity-verification data.

NDIA-ICT-ING-007
7. Secure engineering and monitoring controls
Secure engineering controls, identity, secrets, encryption and monitoring

Integration code, platforms, identities, credentials, endpoints and data flows must implement secure engineering and control baselines, including secure development, dependency and configuration checks, unique least-privilege identities, approved secret and token handling, encryption and managed keys, gateway and boundary protections, logging and monitoring, Protective DNS or equivalent malicious-endpoint controls, vulnerability disclosure and remediation, cryptography readiness and cyber threat intelligence integration where applicable.
Applies to APIs, middleware, gateways, file and event pipelines, secrets, service accounts, external endpoints and security monitoring for integrations.

8. API and digital service design
API design, interoperability, reuse and service consistency

NDIA integrations and APIs must use approved Australian Government and NDIA design patterns, including OpenAPI specifications, catalogue registration, reusable interfaces where safe and lawful, consistent naming, payload, pagination, error, versioning and lifecycle patterns, controlled change and deprecation, and connection patterns that reduce repeat data requests and support reliable digital services.
Applies to production APIs, reusable interfaces, catalogued integration services and digital services supported by integrations.

9. Cloud, hosting and regulated infrastructure
Cloud, hosting, gateway, regulated infrastructure and resilience

Integrations using cloud, hosting, gateways, Security Service Edge, data centres, connected devices or regulated critical infrastructure services must use approved or certified providers where required, review current IRAP or equivalent assurance, define shared cloud controls and sovereignty or data residency risks, protect internet-connected and classified flows through approved gateway or SSE capabilities, maintain exit, portability and continuity arrangements, identify SOCI and Systems of Government Significance obligations and third-party data processing notifications, and include critical assets in required risk management programs.
Applies to cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway, Security Service Edge, data platform, connected-device, Systems of Government Significance and SOCI-relevant integrations.

NDIA-ICT-ING-010
10. Supplier, procurement and contract controls
Supplier, procurement, contract and assurance controls

Procurement, contracts, interface agreements and supplier onboarding for integration services must assess whole-of-life value and security, privacy, hosting, records, accessibility and supply-chain risks; use secure and verifiable suppliers; include proportionate control clauses and flow-down requirements; require evidence, audit rights and IRAP or equivalent assurance where relevant; manage foreign ownership, control or influence, subcontracting, offshore access and lifecycle risk; and define secure transition, termination, data return or destruction and access revocation.
Applies to all purchased, outsourced, managed, partner and supplier-supported integration products and services through procurement, operation, renewal and exit.

Incident response, breach notification and cyber/crisis reporting

Integration owners and suppliers must detect, escalate, preserve evidence for, contain, notify and recover from security, privacy, data quality, ransomware, cyber extortion, safeguarding and critical infrastructure incidents within agreed timeframes, including assessment of Notifiable Data Breach, Cyber Security Act, SOCI, provider and whole-of-government coordination or reporting obligations, and must track lessons learned and control improvements to closure.

Applies to all integration incidents; additional reporting applies when statutory thresholds, supplier or provider obligations, safeguarding obligations or cyber-crisis coordination requirements are triggered.

Records, retention, FOI, auditability and transparency

Integrations must create and preserve reliable records and audit trails showing exchanged data, source, recipient, timestamp, purpose, authority, sensitivity, version, outcome and system or user activity; retain or dispose of records only under approved authorities; support export, FOI, privacy, audit and legal retrieval and explanations; and publish appropriate operational information without exposing sensitive security, privacy, commercial or partner information.
Applies to integration records, payload stores, logs, configuration, metadata, policy information and documents held by NDIA, suppliers or partners.

13. Accessibility and inclusive use
Accessibility, inclusive communications and non-discrimination

Participant or public-facing integration journeys, generated content, notices and authentication flows must be accessible, inclusive and easy to understand, meet applicable WCAG and Australian Government accessibility requirements, provide clear support paths and approved alternatives, and include accessibility requirements in design, testing, procurement and acceptance criteria.
Applies to user-facing services, notifications, messages, documents, identity journeys and supplier components produced or supported by integrations.

14. Data governance, quality and matching
Data governance, quality, matching and Indigenous data safeguards

Integration datasets must have accountable data owners, approved definitions, schemas, validation rules, lineage and lifecycle controls; critical integrations must reconcile failed, duplicate, stale or conflicting records; data matching must have an approved purpose, authority, protocol, minimum fields, secure transfer, quality thresholds, transparency, human review and statutory-regime compliance; and integrations involving Indigenous data must apply culturally safe governance and safeguards.
Applies to all shared datasets, source-of-truth and reference data, data matching programs, reconciliation processes and Indigenous data handled by integrations.

16. Fraud, integrity and investigation controls
Fraud, transaction integrity and investigation

High-risk integrations that create, change, validate or analyse provider, financial, entitlement, payment or participant data must include fraud, corruption and integrity controls by design, including input validation, segregation of duties, exception handling, anomaly detection, monitoring, recovery support, tamper-evident investigation records and authorised investigator access.
Applies to integrations supporting payments, provider claims, entitlement decisions, eligibility, plan transactions, compliance analytics or fraud and integrity monitoring.
